title: Marquise Brown's 265 Yards at Bedlam in 2017
question: Who holds Oklahoma's single-game receiving yards record?
answer: Marquise Brown caught nine passes for 265 yards in Oklahoma's 62-52 win at Oklahoma State on Nov. 4, 2017, a school single-game record at that time. He topped the 232 yards Dede Westbrook had set in 2016.
summary: Marquise Brown caught nine passes for 265 yards, with touchdowns of 84 and 77, in Oklahoma's 62-52 Bedlam win in 2017, a Sooners single-game record.
body: Marquise Brown set Oklahoma's single-game receiving-yards record on Nov. 4, 2017, when he caught nine passes for 265 yards in a 62-52 win at Oklahoma State. NCAA.com labeled the total the single-game program record, and the Oklahoma State athletics recap of the AP game story called it a school record too.

Two of those catches went for touchdowns, from 84 and 77 yards, both thrown by Baker Mayfield. The 84-yarder in the second quarter was the longest score of the afternoon. Brown had 178 yards by halftime, which tied Juaquin Iglesias' school mark for receiving yards in a half.

The mark topped the 232 yards Dede Westbrook posted against Texas in October 2016, so the record changed hands in barely a year. It also came inside one of the wildest Bedlam games ever played in Stillwater, with Oklahoma outgaining the Cowboys 785 yards to 661.

The teams combined for 114 points, the most in the series' history to that point and well past the 102 from Oklahoma's 61-41 win in 2008. Mayfield threw for a school-record 598 yards, and Brown was the player on the other end of the biggest plays. The Sooners improved to 8-1 with the win.
